inputs.text: RAW photograph, real location photography inside a vast water-carved limestone cave chamber at night, shot on a full-frame digital cinema camera with a 24mm lens at eye level, deep focus, long exposure, natural exposure with true deep blacks and restrained highlights, subtle photographic grain. Cinematic and spacious: a cathedral-scale chamber with a level compacted-earth and wet stone floor open enough for two people to stand and sit apart, a low natural rock ledge at the near left edge, a small still pool reflecting light, eroded rib columns, bedding shelves and folded limestone curtains along the far walls, a dark passage receding into blackness at the back. One motivated light only: a cold steel-blue moonlight shaft entering from a high side opening at a low grazing angle, raking the wet rock with bright specular edges and long shadows, thin cool haze giving the light a visible volumetric path, everything else falling into darkness with faint rock texture. Wet pale-grey limestone with fine geological microtexture, mineral veins, calcite crust, damp patches, sparse drips. No people. Documentary realism, geological survey photograph, National Geographic quality, nothing stylized.
